checks: No eclipse at 25 of 102 covered epochs where the 1.90452 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 342621731 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.904519 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse causes a 1.46% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal stands out strongly in the photometric data with a detection significance of 127.5. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal originates from the target location, though with a centroid offset of 4.5 arcsec. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. One open question remains: the depths of alternating eclipses differ significantly, which could indicate orbital or stellar dynamics affecting the system, though the eclipse timing and pixel confirmation are unaffected by this variation.
